chapter: Hite tours, postwar L.A. and the Central Avenue scene
title: Armstrong records the book wrongly credits to Royal
summary: He did not record Confessin' and Ding-Dong Daddy; it was Les Hite, and the earlier house band was Leon Herriford's.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: (Inaudible). In this book on Basie, there's a sort of chapter on you. There's the specific names of some of the things you recorded like with Louie Armstrong, "Confessin'" and "I'm a Ding-Dong Daddy."
The guy that played the alto on that was Les Height.

Oh. In the book, Count Basie and His Orchestra by ________, it says that during the 1930s, the Height band was frequently called upon to accompany Louie Armstrong on the recordings which the solo trumpet star was contracted to make for the Okay (PHONETIC) label and Marshal Royal was one of the musicians who contributed the background supports for such acknowledged Armstrong classics as "Confessin'" and "I'm a Ding-Dong Daddy." It is interesting to note here that Lionel Hampton and trombonist Lawrence Brown were also in the Height band when it made these records.
I wasn't there. That was done at one of the periods when Louie Armstrong was there, before I started into the band.
But didn't you say earlier that you did record with Louie? (Inaudible).

I just played with him. I wasn't recording with him. I didn't make the records. I wasn't on those at all. That was Les Height playing. The time before when Louis was out there, it was a band by the name of Leon Hereford (PHONETIC) that did the first group of recordings for Louie when he was there. That was the "Song of the Islands" and

things like that. That was -- Leon Hereford was the house band at Sebastian's Cotton Club. Then, when he died, Les Height became the house band for Sebastian's Cotton Club. Lawrence Brown had just gone into the band, having left either one of the -- he had just left Curtis Moseby's Blueblowers (PHONETIC) and he went into the Height band and got there just before I went there. He was an addition to the band. They added one extra trombone player to the band.
So Lawrence is on those records.
Lawrence is on the records. I am not on the records. I the next time he came in.
